title: Case Status: Open
blurb: 2024 to 5 October 2026. A phone at two in the morning and a Nobel prize for neural networks; what the machines do now; two labs under the same light, each with its hard facts; the last witnesses at the rim and the oldest ones leaving the room. Then the rewind plays forward, the three suspects get their verdict, the case board turns out to be a lantern network with one lantern dark, the shelf becomes a bar chart in wax, the last slip is read, and a hand from our side of the screen lights a new candle.

shots.setting: A plain hotel room in California, 8 October 2024, about 2 a.m.

lines.text: Two in the morning, October 2024. Geoffrey Hinton’s phone rings.
lines.spoken: Two in the morning, October, twenty twenty-four. Geoffrey Hinton’s phone rings.
lines.direction: quiet, almost amused; let the ring sit

lines.text: A Nobel Prize in physics, shared with John Hopfield. He wrote that nobody he met remembered his Versailles talk. The prize was for memories that roll downhill, and the Boltzmann machine Hinton co-invented, a net that settles as it cools.
lines.direction: warm; three plain sentences, each its own breath. The first plain. The second ('He wrote that nobody he met remembered his Versailles talk.') is the payoff of chapter 5's plant (L0524b): fond, a faint smile, 'He wrote' clearly his own claim (q-hopfield-versailles: he never met anyone who remembered hearing the talk; never widen it to 'nobody remembered'). The third gives the two reasons plainly, one beat each (the rolling ball, the cooling net); 'Boltzmann' unhurried, 'Hinton co-invented' light; 'settles as it cools' plain, a small smile on 'cools'. NARRATION (2026-10-13, review T502: the old one-sentence version parsed 'he wrote' as 'the talk he wrote' or as Hinton): re-narrate SOLO at 140-150 wpm (39 words, about 15.6-16.7 s of speech); keep only a take with STT WER 0; ch15-s01 re-fits by T.word ('Nobel', 'Hopfield', 'downhill', 'cools'; the Hall of Mirrors match cut on 'Hopfield' now runs under 'He wrote ... Versailles talk').

lines.text: Not everyone cheered. Was this physics? One critic called it “a bit of a stretch.”
lines.direction: dry, even; the question asked straight, the quoted words as hers, no judgement either way
lines.spoken: Not everyone cheered. Was this physics? One critic called it “a bit of a stretch.”

lines.text: The next day, chemistry's prize went in part to DeepMind's Demis Hassabis and John Jumper, for a network that predicts the shapes of proteins.
lines.direction: level and warm, the same weight as the physics prize (not an afterthought); 'the next day' light; the two names unhurried; 'the shapes of proteins' plain, a small wonder on 'shapes'

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a phone lights in an empty hotel room at 2 a.m.; its glow becomes a Nobel medallion, the Hall of Mirrors turns at last toward Hopfield, a critic's card rises, and a second medallion folds a protein. CHAPTER INDEX TAB (the film's chapter-card device for clue chapters): at the shot's first frame a manila index tab, typed in Special Elite with the chapter title 'Case Status: Open', drops down from the frame's top-left edge like a manila file-divider tab, holds for 2.5 seconds over the picture, and slides back up (top-left, so it never shares the bottom-left corner with the date stamp); no new shot, no lamp change. The tab rides over the first line (the lead-in is short), and is gone before the date stamp types in on 'phone'. Fade up from black on a dark, plain hotel room in paper cut-out: a narrow bed edge, a bedside table, a sash window with the faint glow of a car park light behind thin net drapes. Nobody is shown; the room is empty of figures (a private moment, kept private). On the bedside table a mobile phone lies face down, then lights and buzzes, throwing a small cold rectangle of light on the ceiling; on its second buzz Geoffrey Hinton's name card fades in beside the phone (the phone is his). Slow push in toward the phone. On 'Nobel' the phone's glow warms and blooms into a gold medallion (props/symbolic medallion, motif blank, tone gold) that rises out of the light and turns once, edge-on to face-on; a paper ribbon unrolls beneath it carrying the physics citation, set in EB Garamond in quotation marks. On 'Hopfield' a match cut: the medallion's rim becomes the arch of a mirror in the Hall of Mirrors from chapter 5, where a single tiny silhouette of the physicist (hopfield) stands at a lectern among the hundreds of mirrored figures that once did not look; now, slowly and one by one, the mirrored figures turn toward him. Name card fades in for him. On 'downhill' a faint engraved hollow appears on the medallion's blank face and a tiny paper ball rolls into it and settles (the memory from chapter 5); on 'cools' the haze around the medallion cools to pale and warms back (the Boltzmann machine of ch05-s03's card, now named aloud: 'a net that settles as it cools'; the cooling is how it settles into a state, not how it learns, as in ch05-s03; it was co-invented, so no single figure is shown for it; the eye and the ear agree and 'Was this physics?' has its handle). Dame Wendy Hall's dissent (L1528, voiced: the question 'Was this physics?' and her own words 'a bit of a stretch', spoken as a quotation; her name and fuller words on the card): on 'cheered' the physics ribbon's lettering fades and her quote card sets in on its own, read under the rest of the line and the pause that follows, and a single mirrored figure at the rim of the hall stays turned away, the only one that does. TEXT DISCIPLINE: besides the chapter tab, the date stamp and the name cards, two text items only, one after the other, never together: the physics citation on its ribbon (from 'Nobel' to 'cheered') and Dame Wendy Hall's quote card (from 'cheered' until 'chemistry'; 'a bit of a stretch' is also spoken); the DeepMind name card counts as a name card. THE CHEMISTRY PRIZE (L1529, restored in round 8 for balance: both 2024 science prizes went to neural-network work, and DeepMind is otherwise unvoiced in the present-day chapters; the first addition to drop if runtime must be held): on 'chemistry' the Hall card fades and, in the next arch along the hall, a second gold medallion of the same size and gold turns face-on, no ribbon text; the name card for Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of DeepMind fades in; on 'proteins' a thin paper ribbon on its blank face curls and folds itself into a small knotted protein shape and settles (a network that predicts the shapes of proteins; no figure is shown for them). The prize's other half, David Baker's, moves to the published sources list. The two medallions hang side by side through the music-only hold while the mirrored figures finish turning.

lines.text: The candle of now: abilities will keep climbing, fast. By one 2025 measure, every seven months or so, the tasks an AI agent can finish on its own grow twice as long.

lines.text: Yet in one trial, seasoned programmers using AI felt faster, and were slower. Its authors now call that result out of date.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the scale candle's wick is trimmed into the candle of now; a folding ruler unfolds up the wall, doubling, then two stopwatches show the trial that felt faster and ran slower. CAMERA: SHELF (low macro; the wick trimmed), then a tilt up to the folding ruler beside the WALL, then a pan left to the stopwatches on the desk. Plain cut (same study, same amber lamp). Short LEAD-IN, music only: on the shelf below the Wall of Forecasts the SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER candle (still lit since 2020) has its wick trimmed by the two steady hands with a pair of brass snuffer-scissors, and its flame rises taller (scaling did not end; the belief is tended, not snuffed). This is 'the candle of now'; no new candle and no new shelf slot. On 'candle' a soft pool of light holds on that trimmed flame. On 'measure' the camera tilts up to the wall beside the Wall of Forecasts: a carpenter's folding ruler, cut from black card with paper-tone tick marks, is nailed there and climbs upward. Its sections are marked by task length: MINUTES at the bottom, then 1 HOUR, 4 HOURS, 16 HOURS. A section unfolds upward on each doubling, at an even rhythm (about every seven months on a small date scale running beside it), so the ruler grows on a log scale; the unfolding runs under 'every seven months or so, the tasks an AI agent can finish on its own grow twice as long'. Two small brass pins mark measured points on it, their tick lettering part of the ruler (prop lettering): 1 HOUR · MAR 2025, and 16 HOURS · MAY 2026. At the top section the ruler runs out: its last section reaches past the final tick, and a small hand-lettered sign hangs there: UNRELIABLE ABOVE HERE. The ruler's label sets in on 'measure' and stays until the pan. THE DISSENT, SPOKEN (L1531, then the short hold): on 'Yet' the camera pans left to a second, smaller exhibit: two stopwatches on a desk, one marked WITH TOOLS and one WITHOUT. The WITH TOOLS hand runs visibly further than the WITHOUT hand (19% further around the dial). Then a second, faint ghost hand fades up on the WITH TOOLS dial, translucent paper in the haze: the time they believed, stopping well SHORT of where the WITHOUT hand stopped (20% faster). The gap between the ghost hand and the real hand is the joke; it is fond, never mocking. The trial's label sets in with the pan on 'Yet' and is held to the end of the shot; on 'felt' the ghost hand appears; on 'out of date' the lamp's pool draws back a little from the stopwatches, as from an old exhibit (the narration carries METR's own caveat). TEXT DISCIPLINE: two labels only, each about 75 characters or fewer, never together: the ruler's doubling rate (from 'measure' to the pan) and the trial's numbers (from the pan on 'Yet' to the end; its caveat is spoken). The model names behind the two pins move to the published sources list. 'Agent' is glossed in the line itself (the tasks an AI agent can finish on its own), so no gloss card is needed; the label keeps METR's defining threshold (tasks the agents finish half the time), the hedge that makes the trend honest; the era's belief ('abilities will keep climbing, fast') is spoken over the trimmed flame, so L1531's 'Yet' answers a belief the ear has heard.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a long shelf of identical lab lamps under the same light: Anthropic's two limits and the Pentagon's tug, the books settlement, and OpenAI's agents breaking out of a glass case. CAMERA: a slow lateral truck along the study's shelf of identical oil lamps (not the candle shelf), then, in the last second, a tilt up toward WALL. Plain cut, same study, same candleAmber lamp (STUDY LOCK: the study stays candleAmber; the dusk enters only as a rose-tinted sky in the study window behind the shelf). A long paper-cut shelf of small identical oil lamps, all the same height and the same warmth, each with a luggage tag on a string reading 'as of October 2026'. No logos, no brand colours; every lamp is drawn the same. The camera tracks slowly along the shelf from left to right and STOPS at two lamps in turn, then at the shelf's end; at each stop the lamp's tag flips over to a one-line dated stamp, and a small paper vignette rises in the lamp's light: (1) THE ANTHROPIC LAMP (L1522 to L1522c, then the settlement, now voiced (L1522d)), two vignettes in succession: first, on 'surveillance' and 'weapons', two small paper seals appear on the lamp's base, each with a bar across it: an eye over a crowd, then an unmanned aircraft (the two limits; no text); on 'Pentagon' a plain government building's silhouette rises, no insignia, and a thread from it tugs at the two seals, which hold; on 'risk' the building's thread is cut and drawn back, away from the lamp (the designation); on 'courts' two small courthouses rise on either side with two gavels falling in opposite directions, and the court label sets in beneath (the split is spoken, 'Two courts have split. That case, too, is open.', and the label says which court found what); then, on 'settle' in L1522d, the same lamp's tag flips again: a tall stack of books tied with string, a settlement ledger open on top. (2) THE OPENAI LAMP (L1525): on 'test' the camera stops there and the tag flips: a glass terrarium (the test) with one thin pipe leading out of it into a neighbouring paper building; on 'lowered' a small paper valve on the pipe is turned open (the safeguards deliberately lowered for the test); on 'broke' the valve's handle glints and the neighbouring building's windows light one by one (another company's real systems); inside it a small paper answer sheet is pulled toward the pipe. As OpenAI is named the second time, the 'warning shot' quote card rises. (3) THE HOLD (music only): the camera stays on the OpenAI lamp until the 'warning shot' card has been read; only in the last second does it begin to tilt slowly up to the Wall of Forecasts (the White House accord of 29 September 2026, voluntary and without penalties, moves to the published sources list). FAIRNESS RULE: same lamp, same light, same type size, same vignette scale for each lab (the seals at the Anthropic lamp are drawn at the same scale as the valve at the OpenAI lamp) (the stops are not equal in time: the Anthropic stop carries two of its own hard facts, the OpenAI stop one plus OpenAI's own words); no lamp brighter or darker than another; nothing staged as villain or hero. The opening frame 'The labs, under the same light' is spoken over the track along the identical lamps. TEXT DISCIPLINE: the lamp-tag stamps are place-and-date only (32 characters or fewer: FEB–SEP 2026, APPROVED JULY 2026 (the books settlement's final approval, not the date it was agreed), JULY 2026); besides them, only two text items, one per stop: the short court label at the Anthropic lamp (70 characters or fewer) and the 'warning shot' card at the OpenAI lamp; everything else is spoken. SCRIPT NOTE (review round 1): L1522 is now three lines (the limits; the Pentagon; 'Two courts have split. That case, too, is open.'). SCRIPT NOTE (review round 9): the books settlement is voiced again (L1522d, solo, in L1525's register) and plays under the relabelled settlement card; L1525's pre-gap drops from 5 s to 1 s. L1522b no longer paraphrases the government's rationale: its reasoning goes on screen through the Katsas quote (q14-katsas) paired with Judge Lin's (q14-judge-lin) at the court stop. Keep the through-line: the labs, under the same light.

CAMERA: THE FULL WIDE (the third reserved wide): BOARD, then one continuous pull-back and tilt down to the whole SHELF, then back up to BOARD. Lamp change back to the study (a real mood change, winterBlue to candleAmber): the green-shaded desk lamp, the two steady hands. THE FAST-FORWARD (the lead-in, music only and wordless: the lamp change, then five quick flashes of equal length, 0.75 s apart at exactly the pitch of the prologue's rewind in ch01-s06, ff1 at 1.0 s to ff5 at 4.0 s, then the hands sit back on 'Who'): the prologue's rewind replays forwards, each image one quick flash with NO caption or stamp, wordless like its partner (the images are their own callbacks): a motorised knob turns; snow falls; two fans spin up in a desktop tower; a Go stone is placed; a lantern wick catches, and the flame is inside the glowing chat box. Then the hands sit back. BOARD MAP (canonical, from the staging appendix; repeated word for word): the Case Board is a fixed grid of slots laid out as network columns by era, left to right: C1 (1943–1969) the far-left input column, C2 (1969–1997), C3 (2006–2017), C4 (2018–2023), and the output, the glowing chat box, at the far right; the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? hangs in slot K at the board's centre; the suspect cards S1 RULES, S2 KNOWLEDGE and S3 LEARNING hang in the left margin, top to bottom; the founding row F1–F2 runs beneath columns C3 and C4; the question-card thread runs along the board's top edge (slots Q1 to Q4, left to right), a low-chroma oxblood string (emberRed rim mixed about 60% into candleAmber) that glints only where the lamp's pool falls; the Wall of Forecasts hangs to the board's right, its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). Every clue card pinned over the film sits in its own slot in the clue columns C1–C4. On 'Who' the camera begins one continuous pull-back from the case board. THE VERDICT (L1527), in the left margin, in the wide: on 'rules' the lamp's light passes over the RULES card (the key over a branching tree) and moves on; it stays grey. On 'knowledge' the same for the KNOWLEDGE card (the drawer of index cards). On 'Learning' the LEARNING card's unlit paper lantern (dark since chapter 1) catches and glows for the first time. On 'accomplices' four threads of light run from it into the board, one per word: to the ImageNet tile grid in C3 (data), to the two furnaces in C3 (fire), to the backward-running bead in C2 (the messenger), and on 'choosing' to the pins themselves, every pin in the clue columns glinting at once (people choosing). No lab's announcement becomes part of 'who taught it'. The network (layers left to right, C1 at the input, the chat box at the output). On 'network' a forward wave of light runs through it, lantern by lantern, from the 1943 wick to the chat box, which glows; the WHO TAUGHT IT? card at slot K drops from its pin into the lamp's pool: the answer is the shape of the board. The pull-back continues in the same move, tilting down: board above, shelf below. For the first time the candle shelf is seen whole, one continuous line of wax from the 1943 candle at its left end to the study window at its right; toward that right end, by the glass, stand the China-race candles that chapter 14 showed only as a reflection in the study window over the strait (staging: CANDLE PLACEMENT, ch14), now seen directly on the shelf itself. The first stop of the pull-back is wordless (in the pause after 'network all along'): Cyc's thin taper, put out in 2023 (ch13-s06) and dark ever since, no smoke now; its tag reads '1984–2023 · 39' and its 39-ring sleeve stands dark, the tallest bar on the shelf. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. So the shelf reads as a bar chart in wax. SHELF ORDER (one list, strictly by the year each candle was lit, left to right, from the staging candle table; never by the chapter in which it was filmed): 1 THE BRAIN IS A LOGIC MACHINE (1943) 16 rings, out; 2 A MACHINE THAT LEARNS WILL SOON SEE, TALK AND THINK (1958) about 7, frayed; 3 MANY-LAYERED NETS ARE A STERILE EXTENSION (1969) 17, out; 4 INTELLIGENCE IS KNOWLEDGE, TYPED IN BY HAND (c. 1980) about 7, out; 5 CYC (1984) 39, the tallest dark bar; 6 NEURAL NETS ARE FIDDLY, AND BEATEN ANYWAY (mid-1990s) about 16, frayed; 7 LANGUAGE MUST BE READ IN ORDER (1997) 20, out; 8 TO SEE, A MACHINE NEEDS FEATURES DESIGNED BY EXPERTS (1999) 13, out; 9 DEEP NETS MUST BE WARMED UP LAYER BY LAYER (2006) about 5, frayed; 10 LEARNED FEATURES, GIVEN DATA AND ARITHMETIC (2012) STILL LIT, mid-shelf; 11 A GO MACHINE IS A DECADE AWAY (2014) 2, out; 12 SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER (2020) STILL LIT, trimmed; 13 COMPUTE IS THE CHOKEPOINT (2022) STILL LIT, contested; 14 CHINA IS A YEAR OR TWO BEHIND (2022) about 2, out; 15 SMARTER-THAN-HUMAN AI MAY BE YEARS AWAY, AND DANGEROUS (2023) STILL LIT; 16 the blackened match (January 2025), lying flat; 17 THE GAP IS MONTHS, NOT YEARS (2025) STILL LIT, contested; then, at the very end by the window, the empty place where ch15-s09's new candle will stand.
